KEY MESSAGE 1...Shower chances Thursday evening into Friday
morning, followed by drier conditions Friday.

Clouds are increasing and showers are on the doorstep of
southern New England, crossing the region through this 
afternoon and evening before exiting the coastal waters early 
Friday morning. These showers are associated with a northern-
stream shortwave trough; however, there is less-than-ideal 
forcing over southern New England. Guidance consensus shows the 
best forcing/lift across northern Massachusetts (mainly north of
Rt. 2) and into southern Vermont and New Hampshire. PWATs are 
quite anomalous for mid-September, nearing 2+ inches, which is 
near the maximum of climatology based on sounding climatology at
Chatham. Today's suite of high-res guidance is in pretty good 
agreement that showers move into far western areas of southern 
New England as early as 3-4 PM, approaching the I-95 corridor 
between 7-9 PM. The threat of thunder is low, though not zero. 
There is also a low threat of localized heavy downpours due to 
the anomalous moisture in the atmosphere, but these showers are 
moving at a good pace. Nevertheless, rainfall amounts will be 
highly variable given the showery nature. There is potential for
as much as a half inch of rain in the vicinity of Rt. 2 in 
northern Massachusetts and into southern Vermont and southern 
New Hampshire, with much less the farther south you go.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Drier conditions Friday and Saturday.

A few early morning showers are possible across Cape Cod and the 
Islands; otherwise, a transient high pressure system moving out 
of the southern Canadian Prairies brings a dry stretch of 
weather Friday and Saturday. Seasonably mild temperatures are 
expected Friday, with highs in the middle 70s and elevated dew 
points initially in the lower 60s, though those fall into the 
upper 40s by Friday afternoon. Breezy NW winds in the afternoon 
with gusts 20-25 mph, mainly across the interior. Then a shift 
to more fall-like conditions on Saturday. A chilly start for 
most, with lows in the lower to middle 40s, while urban areas 
remain in the lower 50s. Not out of the question that upper 30s 
occur along the east slopes of the Berkshires and across 
northern Worcester County. Otherwise, a crisp afternoon with 
sunshine and highs in the middle to upper 60s. Light east winds 
will lead to slightly lower temperatures for eastern coastal 
communities, with locations like Boston perhaps not climbing out
of the lower 60s. Dew points in the 40s will add to the crisp 
feel.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Next chance for rain Sunday into Monday. There 
remains uncertainty in the details such as coverage, timing, 
amounts. Showers may linger through early next week.

Still have timing concerns for rainfall Sunday into Monday.
While a high pressure should be moving off the coast Saturday 
night, it may still have too much influence to prevent rainfall
from overspreading our region during the morning. Still favoring
rainfall arriving from west to east Sunday afternoon into Sunday
night. Another high pressure over eastern Canada should become
more of an influence over the course of Monday. Thus, not
certain how many showers will remain Monday morning. Thinking
the greatest risk for lingering showers will be towards the
south coast. 

The potential rain amounts will depend on the exact track of 
this low pressure, which is still variable across guidance this
far out in time. This variance translates quite clearly to the 
rain totals across both deterministic and ensemble guidance.
Moisture should not be that much of a limitation. Overall, 
still looking like another soaking rainfall for most. Favoring 
the highest rainfall totals towards the south coast of New 
England at this time.

The forecast trend is for drier weather Tuesday and Wednesday.
It appears that another low pressure could approach from the
Mid Atlantic states sometime towards Thursday.
